name: git_diff
description: Read-only diff of what has changed, either against the working tree or between two references. Never applies, stages, or reverts anything — see `git_status` for what to run before treating a diff's absence of output as 'nothing changed.'

cwd.description: Directory to run the diff from, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside a git repository.

staged.description: Diff the index against the last commit (what would be committed) rather than the working tree against the index (what is not yet staged).

path.description: Limit the diff to one file or directory, relative to the workspace root. Omit to diff everything changed.

max_bytes.description: Upper bound on diff output. A diff exceeding this is truncated and `truncated` is set — a large diff silently cut off and read as complete is worse than one honestly marked partial.

truncated.description: True if `max_bytes` cut the diff short.

files_changed.description: Count of files touched by this diff, independent of how much of the text was returned.

errors.description: `cwd` does not resolve inside a git repository.
`cwd` or `path` resolves outside the workspace root and was refused before any git command ran.
`path` does not exist in the working tree.

safety_notes: Read-only — no `git apply`, no `git checkout`, no reversal capability exists behind this schema at all. A `truncated` diff must never be summarized as though the visible portion were the whole change; `files_changed` is reported precisely so a truncated diff cannot be mistaken for a small one.
